question.leadin: This government was headed by Philippe Petain.
question.text: Name this Nazi-approved government that ruled France from a namesake city during World War II, while the Germans occupied Paris.
question.answerHtml: Vichy France [or the French State; or État français; prompt on France]
question.clue: A group of 80 members of parliament dubbed for this government voted against the dissolution of the Third Republic.

swap.leadin: The Treaty of Verdun divided this man's lands between Lothair, Charles the Bald, and Louis the German.
swap.text: Name this son of Pepin the Short, a Frankish king who conquered much of Western Europe.
swap.answerHtml: Charlemagne [or Charles I or Charles the Great; or Carolus Magnus; prompt on Charles]
swap.clue: This man commissioned a namesake book rebutting Second Nicaea by Theodulf, who with Bavarian envoy Arno of Salzburg and Alcuin of York formed the core of this man's imposing royal court.

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about a student protest.
question.text: In 1968, student protesters in this city clashed with police in the Latin Quarter. A massive strike ensued, and Jacques Chirac was sent to negotiate with workers.
question.clue: In 1968, a wave of protests that grew out of the Sorbonne universities forced Charles de Gaulle to flee this city.

swap.leadin: This period during the French Revolution was sparked by the promulgation of the Law of Suspects.
swap.text: Name this time during the French Revolution when thousands of "enemies of the Revolution," including Marie Antoinette, were guillotined.
swap.clue: It was marked by legislation like the Law of Suspects and by incidents like the noyades, where priests and nuns were tied together and drowned.

question.leadin: This emperor defeated Franz Joseph I at the Battle of Solferino.
question.text: Name this French emperor who also allied with Sardinia to win the Battle of Magenta. This leader's military successes were stopped after he abdicated following the Battle of Sedan.
question.answerHtml: Napoleon III [or Charles Louis Napoleon Bonaparte; do not prompt on “Napoleon”]
question.clue: Together with Camilo Cavour, this man concluded the secret agreement of Plombiers, and assistance to the Piedmontese in the victory over Austria at the Battle of Solferino resulted in the Peace of Villafranca.

swap.text: This founder of the Carolingian dynasty was victorious at Tours. His grandson would go on to be the first Holy Roman Emperor.
swap.clue: He served as Mayor of the Palace in Austrasia, a title he passed to his son, Pepin III after securing another victory at the Battle of Cologne.

question.leadin: The tide of this battle is alleged to have turned when the losing side ran from the battlefield in order to protect their camp and all the loot inside.
question.text: Name this battle in which Frankish infantry defeated forces under Abd ar-Rahman. It took place after an appeal by Odo the Great as an invading force approached the River Loire.
question.answerHtml: Battle of Tours (or the Battle of Poitiers; or the Battle of the Palace of the Martyrs)
question.clue: The losers of this battle were led by Abd el-Rahman, who died during it.

swap.leadin: A ruler from this dynasty fought three civil wars against his sons after they accused his wife Judith of Bavaria of infidelity.
swap.text: Name this medieval dynasty. The queen Bertrada from this dynasty pushed her son Carloman out of power to help her other son Charlemagne.
swap.clue: A member of this dynasty granted the territory of the future Papal States to Stephen II in a so-called "donation."

question.text: This dynasty lends its name to a variant of Latin script used in many 8th century manuscripts. This dynasty was founded by Clovis I in 509.
question.clue: These kings all had long hair and gave power to regional "mayors of the palace" after Dagobert I's rule.

swap.text: A king of this name, known as the Quarreller, ruled Navarre in the early fourteenth Century. Kings of this name from another country include ones known as "The Fat" and "The German."
swap.clue: The Albigensian Crusade ended during Blanche of Castile's Regency for another king of this name, who was canonized after leading the Seventh and Eighth Crusades.

question.leadin: Emmanuel Le Roy Ladurie's microhistory of the village of Montaillou studied the records of some of the last people accused of this heresy.
question.text: Name this heresy, alleged to consist of a dualism between good and evil, supposedly led by a spiritual elite known as the perfecti.
question.clue: Emmanuel Le Roy Ladurie examines the methodic search for members of this heresy in the title town of his work Montaillou.

swap.leadin: It is said that St. Anselm elected not to join its namesake monastic congregation when he realized how little time would be left for his personal study.
swap.text: Identify this congregation, named for an abbey, which was founded in 909 when William the Pious gave his Burgundian hunting grounds to the Church and first led by abbot Berno of Baume.
swap.clue: Cardinals Richelieu and Mazarin both led this institution while serving as ministers to the kings of France.

question.leadin: The period at the end of the Republican Calendar was named for this term.
question.text: Give this term that referred to the working class during the French Revolution. It derives from the tendency for lower-class people to wear trousers instead of breeches.
question.clue: The five days at the end of the French Revolutionary Calendar, which were not part of any month, were originally named for this group.

swap.leadin: This man gained a fiefdom from King Charles the Simple with the signing of the Treaty of Saint Clair-sur-Epte.
swap.text: Name this father of William Longsword and wife of either Poppa or Gisela. His conversion to Christianity gave him control of a certain French region, though by the time he died, he had to massacre a hundred Christian prisoners to keep himself sane.
swap.clue: In some sources this man was known as 'Ganger' or 'walker' because he was too large to mount a horse, and he is said to be the son of the earl of More, while the more dubious Dudo of St. Quentin claims that he came from 'Dacia', probably indicating Denmark.

question.leadin: This woman's father, Francis II, was required to get the permission of the King of France in order to marry her off by terms of the Treaty of Sable ending the "Mad War."
question.text: Name this woman, who ended her engagement to Maximilian I when the king became concerned about his realm being encircled by a powerful political couple.

swap.leadin: This historian was executed by the Gestapo for his work in the French Resistance.
swap.text: Name this co-founder of the Annales School of history with Lucien Febvre. He is noted for his posthumous text The Historian's Craft and for various books on French rural society.
swap.clue: A study by this man, which documented popular belief in a cure for scrofula, was titled The Royal Touch.

question.leadin: This arch-conservative ideology, which formed after the July Revolution, was opposed to republicanism, Bonapartism, and Orleanism.
question.text: Name this political alignment from the July Monarchy onward whose adherents included Honore de Balzac. Partisans of this ideology supported the restoration of the Bourbon dynasty to the French throne.
question.clue: Portions of the Protocols were plagiarized from the Dialogue in Hell Between Machiavelli and Montesquieu, a work by Maurice Joly advancing this royalist position, contrasted with the Orleanists and the Bonapartists.

swap.leadin: Despite not being involved in this event, the charlatan Alessandro Cagliostro was prosecuted after it came to light.
swap.text: Name this scandal at the 18th-century French court, which resulted in the arrest of Jeanne de la Motte and the Cardinal de Rohan.
swap.answerHtml: Affair of the Diamond Necklace [or Affaire du Collier de la Reine]
swap.clue: This scandal was orchestrated by Jeanne de la Motte, who pretended to be a countess to scam people during this scandal.

question.leadin: Name these historians who wrote on the French Revolution, FTP each.
question.text: Chair of French Revolutionary history at the Sorbonne from 1937-45, his two-volume The French Revolution ushered in a Marxist approach to the entire era.

swap.leadin: The main thrust of this program was to have monasteries directly responsible to the Pope instead of local rulers, so as to avoid simony and lay investiture.
swap.text: Identify this movement begun by Saint Odo and Duke William at the namesake abbey in Aquitaine.
